rows.scope: Table ב (cadmium) row 2: שומנים, שמנים ותחליבי שומן (מסוג מים בשמן) [fats, oils and fat emulsions (water-in-oil type)]
rows.basis: mg/kg of the food as listed; instrument states no wet/dry or as-sold basis. General notes 1-2: a listed food used as a raw material must comply before incorporation; a finished product is assessed pro rata to its raw-material share.
rows.successor: Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as adopted into Israeli law under the Public Health Protection (Food) Law 5776-2015 s.3a / Second Schedule A item 1 (Amendment 10, 4 Aug 2024; the 1881/2006 adoption it replaced was in force from 1 Jan 2023). EU text carries no Cd ML for fats and oils, so this cell has no direct successor value.
rows.evidence: Row 2 '0.03' under 'להלן הכמות המרבית של קדמיום במזון (מ"ג לק"ג)'; PDF p.3 (table ב)
rows.primary_source_used: /Users/karenpendergrass/Desktop/heavy-metal-index/raw/regulatory/il/israel-moh-fcs-2016-heavy-metals-tin-food.pdf (sha256 7c0521c5…f057883; title 'עדכון קווים מנחים רמות מקסימום למתכות כבדות ובדיל -1.5.2016'); in-force check: https://www.gov.il/he/departments/policies/fcs-reg-01022007 (browser render)
rows.note: Number and scope CONFIRMED (0.03 mg/kg = 30 µg/kg; row wording matches the register's translation). Mismatch is on in-force status only: the MoH policy page hosting the register URL is titled 'לא בתוקף - קוים מנחים לכמות מרבית של מתכות כבדות במזון' (NOT IN FORCE), publication 25.02.2008, updated 19.02.2026. Corroboration: the 2020 extension order (nevo 502_298, s.321(d),(f) of the 2015 Food Law) listed this 01.05.2016 guideline as appendix item 32 and extended it only to 6 Jan 2022; MoH Food Service notice of 26 Aug 2024 records the adopted EU contaminants regulation in force in Israel since 1.1.2023 and 2023/915 (text as at 25.04.2024) as its replacement; 2025 orders/notices apply the 2024-2025 EU amendments. Direct fetch of the gov.il blob returned HTTP 403, so the held copy (title matching the 1.5.2016 update) was used for the text. The policy page's only attachment href is exactly the register URL (…/BlobFolder/policy/fcs-reg-01022007/he/files_databases_fcs_regulations_Reg_01022007.pdf), so the 'not in force' flag attaches to this document specifically.

rows.scope: Annex I, 3.2.14.7 'Cephalopods' (under 3.2.14 'Fishery products and bivalve molluscs')

Later amendments located by search (Reg. (EU) 2026/1825 on 3-MCPD/GE and 2026/1890 on furans, both 29 Jul 2026) do not touch Annex I section 3.2.14; the register's un-dated CELEX URL should point at the consolidated text.

rows.scope: Annex I, 3.2.14.5 'Crustaceans' (under 3.2.14 'Fishery products and bivalve molluscs')
rows.basis: Wet weight (3.2.14 remark); applies to muscle meat from appendages and abdomen (cephalothorax excluded); for crabs and crab-like crustaceans (Brachyura and Anomura) to muscle meat from appendages; Article 3(1)-(2) for dried/diluted/processed/compound food.
rows.evidence: 3.2.14.5 'Crustaceans 0,50 … muscle meat from appendages and abdomen'; consolidated 08.10.2025 p.47
rows.primary_source_used: /Users/karenpendergrass/Desktop/heavy-metal-index/raw/regulatory/eu/eu-2023-915-consolidated-2025-10-08.pdf (EUR-Lex consolidated text 02023R0915, as amended through M10 = Reg. (EU) 2025/1891, consolidation date 08.10.2025)
rows.note: 0,50 mg/kg = 500 µg/kg; wet-weight basis matches the row. The scope is narrower than plain 'crustaceans': the ML attaches to appendage/abdomen muscle meat only (brown meat/cephalothorax excluded); a register note to that effect would be useful. Consolidation used: 08.10.2025; 2026 amendments (2026/1825, 2026/1890) do not touch 3.2.14.
